canal_p15_001.speaker: narrator
canal_p15_001.text: The thirty-fifth morning began with a smaller local reading, then another smaller one an hour later. The public water officer kept both observed falls before accepting a new lower assessment. The branch still held reeds across the seasonal turn. Brown water lay in the house yard, and the planted rows remained partly covered. Luo read the current account to the higher shelter before describing possible work. A falling mark gave them another question to ask, not permission for everybody to run home together.

canal_p15_002.speaker: narrator
canal_p15_002.text: Bao's wrist stayed supported after breakfast. He could move his fingers lightly, but ordinary grip still hurt. The clinician's restriction barred loaded work, and his reassigned emergency hours belonged to the road crew now. He looked over the guide drawing from his chair and noticed the private close board's small handle stood opposite the public return's movement. Two neighboring controls had different jobs. Yue marked their directions on the receiving sketch so somebody arriving after the storm would not move both merely because they faced one channel.

canal_p15_003.speaker: narrator
canal_p15_003.text: The garden owner wanted the public return opened fully as soon as the branch moved. Her tenant wanted the private outlet checked first because ordinary yard water had no other way to leave. The bean gardener wanted the fastest possible fall at his rows. They were not disagreeing about whether water should go. They were disagreeing about which current risk should decide the first movement. Luo asked the officer to show the actual sequence his observed head permitted instead of letting the loudest loss become the channel's operating instruction.

canal_p15_004.speaker: narrator
canal_p15_004.text: From the protected high station, the officer measured the branch's reachable end and its current angle against the reed mass. It could be drawn toward a shallow exposed edge using his department's checked line-and-brake gear, anchored on actual sound ground above the flow. The gear's accepted load covered this assessed branch under the current bounded pull, not an entire tree against any current. His standing duty appointment and owned equipment supplied that task. The canal's small actuator would stay separate from the branch clearing.

canal_p15_005.speaker: narrator
canal_p15_005.text: The officer's ordinary crew inspected the line path and checked the brake before loading it. No rope went around a person's body. The anchor used the rated ground fixture already at the public upper approach, whose present seating passed the accessible inspection. The old quarry reports remained upstream context, not the source of any strength in the gear. Yue watched the crew point to each actual working position. The clearing plan looked disappointingly slow until she noticed how little of its load depended on a person trying to be stronger.

canal_p15_006.speaker: narrator
canal_p15_006.text: The road workers served as ground receivers within their revised remaining paid intervals. They kept the higher path clear and relayed the officer's actual stop call to the canal watchers. Yue observed the house yard from its sound mark rather than joining the hauling line. Jiang stood at the isolated small apparatus with its accepted current record. Their jobs occupied the same morning without becoming one enormous magical operation. The branch would move through ordinary rated gear, the gates through their own checked conditions and people through the ground still under their boots.

canal_p15_007.speaker: narrator
canal_p15_007.text: Han asked whether the officer's line could pull his mother's chest from the lower shed after the branch cleared. The officer said his current appointment concerned the public obstruction and would end at its actual task limit. A private retrieval would need its own present access assessment and arrangement. Han did not argue. He asked the store worker to mark where the chest stood inside so later recovery could avoid blind searching. The man remembered its exact wall. Their new handover conversation had already made one future private task easier.

canal_p15_008.speaker: narrator
canal_p15_008.text: The first controlled pull moved only the branch's loose outer leaves. Its thicker fork stayed caught below the visible reed bundle. The officer stopped and held the brake in its accepted position while his observer examined the current change from sound ground. He would not increase the pull merely because something moved. Yue saw brown water slip through the new narrow opening and heard the gardener cheer too soon. The actual branch remained caught, and its released leaves had made the view less clear rather than the job complete.

canal_p15_009.speaker: narrator
canal_p15_009.text: A reed knot tightened against the branch fork under the changed angle. The officer adjusted the line's reachable attachment only after unloading the pull and confirming the safe working reach at the exposed edge. His crew used an ordinary hooked pole from sound ground, never stepping into the run. The new angle brought the assessed fork toward its shallower release. Yue checked the yard mark and called a small fall. The report pleased the tenant, but nobody treated it as permission to open the private board before its own current head was read.

canal_p15_010.speaker: narrator
canal_p15_010.text: The second pull eased the branch onto the exposed shallow edge inside the accepted line load. The brake held its changing weight while the crew secured it clear of the public return. Loose reeds began passing through the reopened turn. The spreader carried a more visible fall toward the basin. The officer checked the actual branch and detached the line only after it rested on its sound support. Yue heard the difference in moving water, louder and less trapped. The gardener stopped cheering and watched the rows quietly.

canal_p15_011.speaker: narrator
canal_p15_011.text: The house yard's mark fell after the return cleared, but a small pool remained beside the ordinary outlet. The tenant asked whether that meant the private pipe was broken again. Bao's earlier accessible inspection found a sound reachable length; today's visible water did not explain the buried part by itself. The officer read the outlet's current receiving level and found it still too high to give the whole yard a free fall. Waiting for another measured decrease might do more than opening a cover under wet ground.

canal_p15_012.speaker: narrator
canal_p15_012.text: Luo kept the private close board at its accepted current position while the public return drained under observation. The owner wanted to lift it and see if water hurried away. The little board had been designed to separate ordinary crossing flows within its small head. It was not an emergency pump, and changing it under unobserved backpressure could send a new run toward the room. Yue drew the two controls with their current states in broad plain lines. The owner's impatience softened when she could finally point to the difference herself.

canal_p15_013.speaker: narrator
canal_p15_013.text: The officer's first report accepted the branch clearing and current public return, preserving the assessed head, load and working positions. His department crew finished that standing duty interval and would return for its own scheduled check later. The canal could not retain them for every private object now exposed by falling water. Luo received the actual report and kept the lower household return conditional on ground and outlet inspection. People in the shelter had another piece of good news with a visible edge around it.

canal_p15_014.speaker: narrator
canal_p15_014.text: The gardener wanted to inspect the drowned rows from the foot crossing. The current board remained above some shallow flow, but its outer approach had not yet passed the post-flood footing check. The road receiver kept it closed and offered the higher view for actual visible-loss mapping. The man said he had waited long enough to know what happened. Yue agreed that he deserved the count, then showed him the unexamined soft edge where a boot could make another loss. He sat down beside the report and began marking rows he truly could see.

canal_p15_015.speaker: narrator
canal_p15_015.text: The reed gatherer looked toward his torn shelter roof and asked the shed receiver to extend his temporary bed until the lower path reopened. The receiver accepted two more nights from the space already assigned, with its usual clear-passage condition. His cutter remained dry. The forgotten spoon might still lie beneath the old roof. He wanted a later retrieval time rather than another promise of sympathy. Luo added his object request to the current return list, after actual people and footing. It would have a place when the route became a route again.

canal_p15_016.speaker: narrator
canal_p15_016.text: Tian took the grandmother's son to see the repaired shutter from the higher view, where the house wall rose above the pooled yard. The shutter stayed closed, and its new latch could still be seen through the gap. He felt relieved enough to laugh at his morning plan to raise the whole wall. Tian told him a useful little shutter deserved relief too. He asked whether she could stitch a better sack strap before his mother used it again. She gave him an ordinary quote and asked his mother first.

canal_p15_017.speaker: narrator
canal_p15_017.text: The grandmother preferred the existing strap padded with a small approved cloth piece rather than a whole new bag. Her son paid Tian's stated small stitching charge from his personal coins. The emergency cover stock remained untouched. Yue watched the old light sack return with its familiar shape and a softer handle. A precautionary departure had become a household task that could improve before the next one. The cup inside still had three legs on its painted bird, and nobody thought the extra leg needed correcting.

canal_p15_018.speaker: narrator
canal_p15_018.text: At the apparatus station, Jiang checked the now-falling local head and actual ground access before opening the case. The small pocket had remained emptied and isolated after yesterday's response. A fresh bounded comparison could verify its side-release after the wet interval while the outside return had its own observer. This would spend some charge only if the current task justified it. Yue's actual route baseline had recovered to its earned second-pair state. She stood beside the unpowered tile and waited for Jiang's current inspection rather than practicing while people discussed larger water.

canal_p15_019.speaker: narrator
canal_p15_019.text: The accepted task would fill the little pocket only to its existing low check mark, then perform the small controlled response into the now-observed clear catch. Jiang allotted twelve supply units across the current check and any required closing comparison, with the actual gauge to show what was used. The conservative available floor was two hundred fifty-six after yesterday's possible twenty-unit draw; higher actual branch counts stayed separate. The supply was ample for this rated small job. It would not buy a higher head or erase the missing broader flood acceptance.

canal_p15_020.speaker: narrator
canal_p15_020.text: Yue felt ashamed of being excited for another command after seeing the house yard wet. Jiang asked whether excitement made her current route less recovered. It did not. She asked whether it permitted skipping a head reading. It did not. Yue said she wanted both the useful job and the pleasure of performing it. Jiang accepted that answer more easily than Yue expected. Pleasure could exist beside the exact task, so long as it did not change the conditions everybody else had to trust.

canal_p15_021.speaker: narrator
canal_p15_021.text: Luo checked the small feeder and confirmed its current hand-controlled low notch. The pocket's independent reference matched its ordinary ruler. Bao watched from his supported chair at the higher station, outside the work position, able to see without gripping anything. The road receiver kept the catch clear during his accepted interval. Nobody made the injured carpenter stand to prove his report still mattered. Yue took the prepared place and heard the actual ready calls, familiar enough now that their absence would have been noticeable.

canal_p15_022.speaker: narrator
canal_p15_022.text: The low fill reached its checked mark without a new wick line or brace shift. Jiang called for the single prepared selection after the independent head check. Yue formed the quarter-unit command within the established half-unit delivery allowance, following the recovered arm path she had actually earned. The selector opened the little side-release; its external actuator took eight counted units. Water moved into the observed clear catch. Yue released at the planned point and let her routes settle while the crew watched the ordinary drain finish.

canal_p15_023.speaker: narrator
canal_p15_023.text: Jiang used four additional units for the accepted closing comparison after the pocket emptied, then isolated the supply. The ordinary geared manual equivalent completed its own unloaded check without a further powered draw. Twelve actual units had been used, leaving a conservative floor of two hundred forty-four while every precise trial and response remainder stayed in the signed gauge. Bao said the little device sounded healthy from his chair. Jiang accepted the current evidence, not its pleasant sound. Yue copied the exact receiving state after her hands steadied.

canal_p15_024.speaker: narrator
canal_p15_024.text: The private outlet's receiving level finally fell below its observed yard threshold near noon. The owner wanted the little close board lifted now. Bao could explain its current intended movement but remained barred from gripping the handle. The actual appointed operator would perform it only after the public return and ground access passed their fresh check. Luo set that near task for the next lower work interval. One controlled pocket could be accepted while the household board still waited. Two neighbors sharing water did not have to receive the same permission at the same time.

canal_p15_025.speaker: narrator
canal_p15_025.text: The weather report showed ridge rain easing while the local fall continued. The officer asked for another fixed reading before allowing broader public walking access. The canal's road receiver had remaining revised hours for ground checking and controlled return; the qualified operator's remaining emergency reporting hours would close her appointment after the actual handover. Yue's original repair days still had later observation tasks, separate from today's two emergency equivalents. Their accounts would need closing without hiding unused or transferred time inside the relief people felt now.

canal_p15_026.speaker: narrator
canal_p15_026.text: At the higher landing, three follow-ups could determine how tomorrow's return would feel. The road crew needed the house approach examined before the little board moved; the gardener wanted a careful visible crop-and-route record; Jiang wanted the wet apparatus's final condition and actual supply chain of counts checked for handover. Every job had an actual receiver and time. Yue could stay close to the house, close to the injured livelihood or close to the device that had given her one small moment of pride amid water much larger than her.

canal_p15_027.speaker: narrator
canal_p15_027.text: Bao asked Yue to choose without trying to compensate for his injured wrist by doing all three jobs. She started to deny that she was, then stopped. His unused hours were already reassigned, and his ordinary later restrictions would remain after supper. The public clearing had succeeded through another qualified crew's gear. Her small command had succeeded within its own allowance. The next task did not need to prove she could repair the whole night. It needed attention given to one real thing while other people did their own work.

canal_p15_028.speaker: narrator
canal_p15_028.text: At the higher landing, the grandmother asked whether her house now had two gates because the canal liked complicated things. Luo showed her the public return on one drawing and the small private crossing control on another. The woman said she cared less about their names than who would come when one stuck. The receiving sheet named both actual keepers under their different duties. She folded it beside the sack, satisfied by a practical answer that did not require learning somebody else's entire profession.

canal_p15_029.speaker: narrator
canal_p15_029.text: The local water had fallen enough to ask about return, but current lower access remained controlled. Yue could inspect the house approach with the road crew, map the gardener's actual visible losses or finish Jiang's wet apparatus handover. The private close board waited for its own checked ground and head. The protected public return was already moving water. One channel had begun serving two distinct controls again, and every person beside it still had a different reason to hope that tomorrow would be ordinary.

choices.text: Inspect the house approach and private outlet.
Map the gardener's actual visible loss.
Finish the wet apparatus handover with Jiang.

canal_p15_030.speaker: narrator
canal_p15_030.text: The road leader took Yue down the checked higher approach after the officer accepted its current falling mark. The inner strip remained closed beyond their examination line. The house yard held shallow puddles and scattered silt, with no person authorized inside until the footing passed. Yue carried the owner's offered doorway drawing and compared its visible step with the real ground. The low stool lay overturned against the wall. It looked like an ordinary thing waiting to be picked up, which made the closed limit suddenly harder to respect.

canal_p15_031.speaker: narrator
canal_p15_031.text: The step's outer edge had shed a small patch of mortar, exposing the stable inner stone. The leader tested from sound ground with his ordinary probe and marked the reachable dry entry. The doorway still required its own support check before a returning person carried anything heavy. Yue wrote the observed patch rather than saying the whole foundation failed. The owner read that distinction at the higher mark and asked when the qualified mason could assess it. Luo sent the actual request through the ordinary property receiver.

canal_p15_032.speaker: narrator
canal_p15_032.text: The private outlet's accessible cover remained on its support after the water fell. A little reed debris lay against the outside mouth, reachable from the dry examination strip. The appointed operator cleared it with an ordinary hook under the current task, then checked the small close board's head. Its present lower limit permitted the planned hand movement. Yue stood at the observation mark while the operator eased it. No command ran through her own routes a second time today. The ordinary mechanism had its own useful hands.

canal_p15_033.speaker: narrator
canal_p15_033.text: The board moved to its intended low position without a new catch. Water in the yard began leaving through the ordinary private outlet. The operator returned the handle to its specified dry-weather receiving state and checked the movement marks. The garden owner watched the little pool shrink and wanted to call the tenant home immediately. The road leader showed her the still-unexamined interior floor. A draining yard gave the house one good result. It did not certify where an older woman could sleep tonight.

canal_p15_034.speaker: narrator
canal_p15_034.text: Yue asked the owner to name the room she wanted checked first when access reopened. The tenant's sleeping place and high grain shelf mattered most, before the owner's seed cupboard. The grandmother agreed through the nearer messenger. She wanted her cup kept at the temporary room until the sleeping place truly dried. The owner put that instruction beside the property's current return sheet. A lawful landlord could choose inspection order while listening to the person whose ordinary night would be spent inside the answer.

canal_p15_035.speaker: narrator
canal_p15_035.text: A dog barked from the higher path, refusing to cross toward the yard. Its young owner said that proved the house was haunted by the storm. The road leader asked him to keep the animal with his family while the ground remained under assessment. Yue could see silt and a changed scent, enough to explain caution without reading an animal's mind. The boy accepted the ordinary waiting place. Nobody invited the dog onto uncertain flooring as a substitute for the actual inspection still needed.

canal_p15_036.speaker: narrator
canal_p15_036.text: The owner produced the building's old receiving sketch from a dry copy held at her market contact. The original had stayed in the house, but this working copy showed the inner floor support and permitted doorway. The qualified mason's actual return could compare those visible parts. Yue asked where the copy came from and recorded its limitation. It could guide the inspection without claiming every hidden member still matched it after the flood. The owner thanked her for using the paper while keeping the ground important.

canal_p15_037.speaker: narrator
canal_p15_037.text: At the higher mark, the grandmother asked whether the overturned stool could be recovered first. It belonged to her late husband, but she did not ask anyone to enter unexamined ground for it. Yue put it into the retrieval list with its actual visible position. The road leader said it could be lifted from the accepted entry after the doorway support check, if that check passed. The conditional answer disappointed her less than Yue expected. She had watched people leave because words finally meant the actual time available.

canal_p15_038.speaker: narrator
canal_p15_038.text: The appointed operator gave Luo the private board's accepted dry-weather state, reachable outlet clearing and observed yard fall. The operator's current interval belonged to the remaining revised road task, with its completion written before another inspection was requested. Yue delivered the still-pending interior and doorway check to the property receiver. The house now had water leaving and a practical return list. Its tenant remained at the higher room until a real floor, rather than the relief everyone wanted, could carry her bed.

canal_p15_039.speaker: narrator
canal_p15_039.text: At the landing, Yue reported the private outlet's restored ordinary function and the current closed interior. The owner agreed to arrange the mason's next assessment from her separate property maintenance funds, since the public channel repair did not purchase a private room's full post-flood certification. The family's offered guest nights would end before every room dried. She would pay the actual additional lodging through its agreed host rather than let the tenant's need become an unspoken favor. Yue felt the return plan gain both a task and a price.

canal_p15_040.speaker: narrator
canal_p15_040.text: The gardener laid his plot sketch on the higher bench and asked Yue to start with rows still visible. He had harvested the low edge on the warning day, saving several baskets by Han's paid cart. The remaining outer rows stood under muddy water. Their crop record showed planting dates and ordinary purchase costs, not the price of an imagined perfect harvest. Yue copied the actual surviving documents while he named the difference between plants grown, crops gathered and income he had hoped to earn.

canal_p15_041.speaker: narrator
canal_p15_041.text: His daughter brought the little bean she had offered yesterday, now dried at the edge. He said she could keep it for seed if it remained suitable after an ordinary check. Yue laughed when she asked whether the flood had made it stronger. He told her the bean had stayed in her pocket, not the field. The answer made him smile for the first time all morning. A tiny surviving thing could give comfort without becoming evidence that the larger lost rows were somehow compensated.

canal_p15_042.speaker: narrator
canal_p15_042.text: From the sound mark, Yue mapped the actually visible flooded portion and the higher rows still above water. She left the concealed roots and lower yield open for later ground inspection. The gardener wanted the whole outer bed marked lost now so nobody reduced his claim afterward. She asked him to preserve the current observation and later actual assessment rather than decide what unseen roots must have done. He accepted reluctantly after reading his offered concern beside the map. His fear of being dismissed belonged in the record too.

canal_p15_043.speaker: narrator
canal_p15_043.text: The charter's protected seasonal use remained relevant to ordinary cultivation, but it did not automatically decide every damage claim. The current route had been altered by the ridge slide, the private path tiles and the branch obstruction. The upstream quarry had also released stronger runoff. Yue put the dated facts on separate lines with their sources. The gardener said the list made blame look slippery. She said it made the hearing answer actual questions instead of choosing the easiest person to dislike before the water even fell.

canal_p15_044.speaker: narrator
canal_p15_044.text: He asked whether his own tiles would make every lost plant his fault. Their removal had reopened the seasonal entrance before the flood. The observed loss after that came under a changed route and larger runoff. His earlier alteration had its own current consequences and could be considered within its actual scope. Yue did not promise a finding on causes she had not assessed. She kept the tile receipt beside the repair record, where both his expense and the obstruction remained visible. A fair account could contain a mistake without expanding it into everything.

canal_p15_045.speaker: narrator
canal_p15_045.text: The public officer's observed branch report arrived while they worked. It described the obstruction, current assessed clearing load and actual fall afterward. Yue showed the gardener the report's accepted public portion. He pointed to the time water began pooling beside his rows and asked for comparison with his own marked observation. The two times were close, but closeness alone did not measure the lost crop. The hearing would have useful evidence about the sequence, and still need the safe field inspection planned for later.

canal_p15_046.speaker: narrator
canal_p15_046.text: A neighbor accused the gardener of exaggerating because his higher rows looked healthy. He invited her to compare those rows with the outer bed after the route opened. She had remembered only the view from her own doorway. Yue kept the current offered accounts separate until their sources could be checked. The neighbor apologized for calling the whole claim a lie and asked whether she could help sort safe beans later at an ordinary paid rate if the gardener needed it. He said he would decide after seeing what remained.

canal_p15_047.speaker: narrator
canal_p15_047.text: The gardener's daughter wanted to bring her own row count to the hearing. Her father began to say adults would handle it. Yue asked whether she had counted actual planted rows before the storm. She had used sticks beside each family picking turn and could show the map her mother helped draw. The offered count could join the family's records, with its method described. It would not certify the condition of roots today. Her father accepted it, surprised by useful work already done outside the conversations he considered important.

canal_p15_048.speaker: narrator
canal_p15_048.text: They finished the visible-loss map with the current high rows, covered outer rows and saved harvest entered separately. The gardener kept his originals. The hearing receiver would receive approved copies before the fortieth-day appointment. Yue added the requested later actual crop inspection, once the footing permitted it. The man had wanted an immediate answer. He now had a sequence in which his work could be seen at more than one moment, instead of being judged by whichever glimpse made another person most comfortable.

canal_p15_049.speaker: narrator
canal_p15_049.text: At the landing, Yue submitted the approved current crop record and its remaining questions. The gardener took his daughter home by the higher route, carrying the little bean in a separate paper fold. The saved baskets would supply actual sales this week; the damaged outer bed would be inspected later. None of that removed his anger about the seasonal use. Yue had learned enough to stop asking his anger to vanish before his evidence became credible. The map remained uncomfortable, and that was one reason it could be useful.

canal_p15_050.speaker: narrator
canal_p15_050.text: Jiang opened the current supply account beside the protected case and asked Yue to read the sequence aloud from the first bench draw. The original six stones had held two hundred forty units. Gate and early bench work left two hundred sixteen before the bounded trial. The actual trial path left its specific remainder. The emergency added eighty, then used two in dry inspection, the precise storm-response draw and twelve today. Yue kept the distinct signed counts rather than replacing them with one smooth invented total.

canal_p15_051.speaker: narrator
canal_p15_051.text: The conservative floor now stood at two hundred forty-four, but the actual gauge could show more because earlier permitted paths used less. Jiang checked the present reading against the actual sequence witnessed by the appointed operators. It matched. The remaining charge belonged to the commission's stones at their assigned store. Yue would not carry a partly used stone as a personal reward for making the small command. She did not want one today. What she wanted was to understand how a useful job could end with resources still waiting for another keeper.

canal_p15_052.speaker: narrator
canal_p15_052.text: They examined the cover after the wet interval. Its tied edge remained clear of the selector, and the contact cap stayed seated. A patch of damp dirt had reached the case's outside handle, away from its protected working contacts. Yue cleaned it with the assigned ordinary cloth while Jiang kept the supply isolated. The task needed no new powered comparison. Jiang said the signed handover should record current accepted mechanical function and the actual remaining supply, with future high-head work still outside its rating.

canal_p15_053.speaker: narrator
canal_p15_053.text: The small side-release's movement marks had not shifted after the repeated low response. Bao had drawn their positions before the sprain, and the current operator compared them without asking his injured hand to make another mark. Yue copied the actual picture for the next keeper. Jiang asked her to separate the public return's branch clearing from the apparatus page. The same morning had supplied both successes, but a tree line and a tiny selector did not acquire one another's capacities by being reported together.

canal_p15_054.speaker: narrator
canal_p15_054.text: Jiang's current emergency reporting hours would complete her two newly paid equivalents after the receiving clerk accepted the handover. No further overnight availability came with that last signature. The road crew's revised remaining intervals carried the ordinary ground checks still agreed. Luo knew the workshop contact for a later fresh appointment if required. Yue asked whether the case could remain in the store while its familiar operator left. Jiang said that was precisely what a stored case often did. Useful equipment did not need to promise a person behind it every minute.

canal_p15_055.speaker: narrator
canal_p15_055.text: At the store, they checked the physical count of eight charged stones against the original six and purchased extra pair. Their actual remaining gauge readings stayed attributed to the present supply record. The unused material stock and weather covers were listed separately from charge. The emergency receiver would reconcile actual labor and material use without valuing stored charge as cash returned to the purse. Yue had once imagined every remaining resource should fit the same kind of balance. The case taught her another ordinary difference.

canal_p15_056.speaker: narrator
canal_p15_056.text: A young landing apprentice asked whether the stones remembered the storm. Jiang said their measured charge changed through the actual apparatus draws, and their outside casings could be inspected for wet damage. Yue could tell a story about the night, but the stones would not certify it. The apprentice looked disappointed. Then he asked to see the ordinary gauge, which was a question Jiang could answer while the case remained safely isolated. They showed him the readable mark from the proper position and kept his hands clear of contacts.

canal_p15_057.speaker: narrator
canal_p15_057.text: Yue compared today's command sensation with her own earlier small work after the actual route had settled. Its stability had improved through preparation and recovery, but it had not opened another pair. Jiang suggested retaining that honest practice note beside the measured delivery record. Yue asked whether it would ever become tedious to write the same earned stage again. Jiang said yes, then gave her the next ordinary recovery instruction. A demanding life could contain a tedious line without making the line false.

canal_p15_058.speaker: narrator
canal_p15_058.text: Before closing the case, Jiang removed her personal plum tin from the bench. It had never belonged to the commission inventory. She offered the last two plums to Yue and Luo, then kept the tin for its familiar lid. Yue laughed at how quickly a comfortable object could look like equipment after sitting near a device. The handover listed eight stones, the actual gauge record and accepted small control parts. It left out tea, plums, future powers and people nobody had hired.

canal_p15_059.speaker: narrator
canal_p15_059.text: At the emergency receiver's desk, Jiang signed her completed current two-equivalent appointment and actual supply condition. Yue delivered the clean sequence of counts and the current device limits. The case would remain at its assigned commission store with no optional object following her personal pack. She felt sad to see Jiang gather her ordinary traveling things. The qualified operator had become a friend during several returns, and friendship had to survive an actual departure rather than keep asking a work order to extend itself.

canal_p15_060.speaker: narrator
canal_p15_060.text: The afternoon reports joined at the canal counter. The private outlet had regained ordinary function, the house interior still awaited its property assessment, the gardener's actual visible-loss map had its later inspection time and the wet apparatus held its precise reconciled charge. Yue knew one follow-up closely and received the others from their workers. The local fall continued under current marks. Two neighboring gates now had distinct accepted states again, while the people waiting for return still needed a room, a row count and a safe path.

canal_p15_061.speaker: narrator
canal_p15_061.text: The garden owner arranged three additional lodging nights, thirty-fifth through thirty-seventh, with the household that hosted both displaced women. She paid its agreed three copper from her separate property maintenance purse, meals included. The earlier four offered nights stayed a gift; this extension was a specific paid arrangement. The tenant did not surrender a damage claim to accept it. Yue delivered the receiving note at their request, glad that a slowly drying floor no longer meant silently stretching another family's pantry.

canal_p15_062.speaker: narrator
canal_p15_062.text: Jiang completed the current reporting handover and took the scheduled local boat after her accepted hours ended. She left the protected case and actual supply record at their assigned store. Yue helped carry her personal plum tin and returned it before boarding. Jiang said the next letter could contain something other than an urgent mechanism problem. Yue said she might describe Tian's plant. The ordinary promise had a known receiver and no deadline borrowed from the storm. Jiang smiled and went aboard while Luo kept the actual departure time in its own account.

canal_p15_063.speaker: narrator
canal_p15_063.text: At the higher shelter, the rescued store worker put on his patched coat and went to his own family's room through the checked ordinary road. Han gave him the paid handling acknowledgment and the amended upper-return procedure. The young man wanted the first future private shift to use that procedure while weather was normal, before another storm tested it. Han agreed. A dangerous missed count had changed a working list. The worker departed without owing his ordinary evenings to everybody who now knew his rescue story.

canal_p15_064.speaker: narrator
canal_p15_064.text: On the thirty-sixth morning, the public officer's repeat fixed reading showed another actual fall. The lower route's current head remained below the observation threshold set for controlled inspection. The road crew accepted the inner approach after its accessible footing check, while keeping the disturbed outer edge fenced. People could reach their properties through a stated dry route at a stated limit. Nobody reopened a whole bank merely because one boot had found firm soil. Yue carried the actual access notice to both receivers before visitors began inventing their own paths.

canal_p15_065.speaker: narrator
canal_p15_065.text: The property mason arrived under the garden owner's separately funded maintenance appointment. He examined the doorway support and accessible interior floor before accepting a light supervised entry. The inner sleeping platform remained sound above the soaked lower boards. Two floorboards had lifted and needed removal, drying and ordinary replacement before the grandmother resumed sleeping in the room. The owner received the actual cost proposal for her own decision. The public spill work had not silently become a private house rebuilding contract.

canal_p15_066.speaker: narrator
canal_p15_066.text: The grandmother entered with the appointed observer only after the light-access check. Her stool could be recovered from the sound entry. She touched it, then asked for the high grain shelf. The replacement millet sack stayed dry where the owner had moved it before warning. Some older kitchen herbs and a low mat were wet. Yue recorded the actually offered household loss, leaving private cupboard contents closed. The woman was relieved, grieving and annoyed at the same time. A room could survive without returning every little thing in it.

canal_p15_067.speaker: narrator
canal_p15_067.text: The owner accepted the mason's ordinary two-board replacement and drying work from her separate property fund. The new paid lodging covered the tenant through its stated interval while that work proceeded. The grandmother chose which dry small objects to take back to the temporary room and left heavy furniture until its actual floor was accepted. Her son helped carry the recovered stool by the marked dry route. He did not add the grain tub merely because his arms could lift it. The route's light limit still mattered after danger looked less dramatic.

canal_p15_068.speaker: narrator
canal_p15_068.text: The reed gatherer reached his old camp under the same controlled lower access and found the carved spoon beneath a folded wet cloth. The torn roof needed ordinary repair before the seasonal shelter could be used again. His higher temporary bed stayed accepted through its stated extra nights. He recorded the actual sailcloth damage for the later review and took the spoon away. Yue saw him smile at a thing worth almost nothing in a market. The large cutter had stayed dry; the small spoon made the place feel his again.

canal_p15_069.speaker: narrator
canal_p15_069.text: The gardener inspected the outer rows after the current foot route passed. Some plants had bent beyond ordinary recovery; others stood dirty but alive. He and his daughter counted actual rows and plants under the agreed method, with an experienced grower checking which could still be harvested safely. The saved higher baskets and new salvage count stayed separate from unharvested loss. Yue copied the approved current result. He apologized again for asking her to count from the distant mark. She said today's count was the reason they waited.

canal_p15_070.speaker: narrator
canal_p15_070.text: The public officer inspected the cleared branch's receiving position and checked that its secured end no longer threatened the return under the current fall. His report preserved the actual obstruction and its removal conditions. The canal's road crew completed its final revised emergency interval after the lower access handover. Together, those accounts explained how people returned and what remained closed. Their tools went back to their actual owners. The thirty-six-copper response would now be reconciled as finite completed labor and received stock, rather than an endless explanation for future work.

canal_p15_071.speaker: narrator
canal_p15_071.text: Bao tried his wrist's ordinary gentle movement and stopped when grip hurt. The clinician's restriction still barred loaded carpentry. He wanted to join the house floor repair because the new boards looked simple. Yue pointed to the actual separate property mason doing that job. Bao laughed sadly at needing to be reminded another qualified person could work while he recovered. His later ordinary commission checks would be revised to light observation only after the clinician accepted it. Nobody promised that the sprain had healed because the water finally fell.

canal_p15_072.speaker: narrator
canal_p15_072.text: Han reached his lower shed through the checked private retrieval route after its own accessible support passed. The personal chest had taken damp at its base. He carried it out with the store worker under the actual load plan, separate from the completed public emergency crew. Some loose household papers stuck together; the little leather shoes lay wet but intact. He opened the lid at the dry store table and sat without speaking. Yue stood nearby until he asked for cloth. The chest had returned, and the loss inside it still needed patience.

canal_p15_073.speaker: narrator
canal_p15_073.text: Pei offered a qualified paper conservator's ordinary contact, not an instruction to peel wet sheets apart immediately. Han could choose that private work at its actual price. He kept the accepted public debt copies safe in their assigned records; the damp personal papers were not the only evidence behind his fifty-six toll claim. Yue helped separate the intact objects from the unopened wet bundle without trying to read household letters. Han wanted his mother's memory restored. The first useful act was refusing to tear it faster for an immediate answer.

canal_p15_074.speaker: narrator
canal_p15_074.text: Tian brought a clean dry cloth for the recovered shoes after Han asked for ordinary stitching advice. Their seams had softened, and drying slowly before handling would help prevent further damage. She charged only for the later repair if he chose it, giving the initial simple advice freely. Han said his mother had once mended a sail badly to prove she could. Tian laughed and said she had made that mistake with a gate seedling. The conversation allowed both people to remember themselves doing foolish things without losing their present dignity.

canal_p15_075.speaker: narrator
canal_p15_075.text: The emergency receiver paid accepted hours after each worker's completion and reconciled the authorized transfer from Bao to the road crew. The labor line remained twenty-four for eight actual equivalents; the material and stone purchases stayed within their eight and four. Stored remaining stock and precise charge stayed with their assigned custodians. The ordinary ninety-six repair account continued toward its own closing checks. No remaining coin from one purse had been invented to compensate every crop or household loss described today. Those claims had their fortieth-day hearing.

canal_p15_076.speaker: narrator
canal_p15_076.text: Luo posted the current ordinary service state beside the controlled lower-return notice. The main gate could resume limited cargo only after its current receiving check; the private close board served its separate dry-weather drainage under its own named receiver. The disturbed outer foot edge remained fenced. People could use what had passed and ask about what had not. Yue read the board in the evening light and liked its plainness. It described a canal still damaged in places, useful in places and no longer offered as a possession of everyone who lived beside it.

canal_p15_077.speaker: narrator
canal_p15_077.text: That evening, the grandmother sat in the temporary room with her recovered stool under her feet and the painted cup on its cloth. Her floor would need more ordinary drying time. The paid lodging had a stated ending, and the owner's private repair had actual accepted tasks. Yue brought the next report time rather than a promise of everything being normal tomorrow. The woman said normal could wait if she knew which door she could enter. Yue left feeling that the ordinary word home had become more precise after the flood.

canal_p15_078.speaker: narrator
canal_p15_078.text: Before sleep, Yue copied the small command's actual recovered-work record beside the crop and house inspection dates. Her earned second pair stayed unchanged. The public line crew had cleared the branch through its own rated gear; the private board had reopened through ordinary hands; her tiny selector response had finished its specific task. On the thirty-seventh morning, they would begin preparing the losses that could be counted for the real hearing, including what common use could explain and what it could never erase by pointing to a charter.
